questions.prompt: Viewed directly ahead at night, which lights identify an ordinary motorized vessel?
answers: A white masthead light and red and green sidelights
Two red lights in a vertical line

questions.prompt: A convoy must give a prescribed sound signal. Which vessel gives it?
answers: Assume the sound signal cancels the give-way duties
questions.explanation: Article 4.01 assigns it to the vessel carrying the boatmaster.

questions.prompt: May a small craft proceeding alone use the general Annex 6 sound signals when necessary?
answers: No, small craft must always be silent
Assume the sound signal cancels the give-way duties
questions.explanation: Article 4.02 provides the small-craft general-signal allowance.

questions.prompt: When may a vessel use another sound for vessel-to-shore communication?
answers: If it cannot be confused with a prescribed signal
Only if it sounds exactly like a prescribed signal
Assume the sound signal cancels the give-way duties
questions.explanation: Article 4.03 prohibits confusing or misusing regulated signals.

questions.prompt: A vessel in distress needs assistance. Which audible signals may it use?
answers: A bell or repeated long blasts
One short and one long once
Assume the sound signal cancels the give-way duties
questions.explanation: Article 4.04 provides bell or repeated long blasts.

questions.prompt: Which overtaking request asks to pass on the starboard side?
answers: Two long followed by one short
Two long followed by two short
One long followed by one short
Assume the sound signal cancels the give-way duties
questions.explanation: The request for starboard is two long and one short.

questions.prompt: After leaving a harbour or tributary, which sound announces an intention to cross the waterway?
answers: One long followed by two short
Assume the sound signal cancels the give-way duties
questions.explanation: Three long blasts announces the crossing under Article 6.16.

questions.prompt: Which pattern identifies a ferry not navigating by radar in reduced visibility?
answers: One long plus four short, repeated within one minute
One long only, repeated every five minutes
Assume the sound signal cancels the give-way duties
questions.explanation: The non-radar ferry signal differs from that for a vessel proceeding alone.

questions.prompt: What must an equipped vessel do before a blind section or narrow channel?
answers: Report on the allocated ship-to-ship channel
Switch off nautical information to avoid interruption
Assume the sound signal cancels the give-way duties
questions.explanation: Article 4.05 requires the report before the specified location.

questions.prompt: Why should temporary navigation notices be checked before departure?
answers: They can change closures, restrictions and operating arrangements
They are only for commercial vessels
Follow the last vessel without checking the current notices
questions.explanation: Temporary directions can materially change the passage plan.

questions.prompt: A sailing vessel starts using mechanical propulsion. For CEVNI classification, what changes?
answers: It is treated as a motorized vessel
It remains a sailing vessel for every rule
Assume every vessel has the same classification
questions.explanation: Mechanical propulsion changes the regulatory classification.

questions.prompt: What course does an Article 6.04 blue board from an upstream vessel indicate to downstream traffic?
answers: A port turn to enter a harbour
A demand to overtake to port
Hold course and speed until the vessels are alongside
questions.explanation: The upstream vessel indicates the passing course under Article 6.04.

questions.prompt: A movable bridge shows red and green together. What is the passage state?
answers: Still prohibited while opening is prepared
Open for passage in both directions
Open only for vessels under 20 m
Enter the opening before confirming it is available
questions.explanation: The mixed display is preparation, not permission.
